title: Veneer vs laminate: which finish suits your home
excerpt: Both can give a handsome finish, but they behave differently. Compare look, cost, care and where each fits best.
author: Comfort Nest Team

content.text: Veneer and laminate are often compared because both cover a plywood base. They are, however, very different materials.

Veneer is a thin slice of real wood, often 0.5 mm, glued to a board. Laminate is a manufactured sheet made from layers of paper and resin, printed with a colour or wood pattern. Veneer is natural, so no two sheets are identical.

Veneer has real grain, depth and the warmth of timber, and it can be polished in different tones. Laminate offers a much wider range of colours, textures and patterns, with consistent results from sheet to sheet.

items: Laminate resists scratches, stains and moisture on the surface and needs only wiping
Veneer needs a protective polish, and can fade or mark if neglected
Veneer can be repolished or repaired; laminate generally cannot
Both rely on the board beneath for water resistance

content.text: Laminate is usually the more economical choice and is quicker to install. Veneer costs more, especially once polishing labour is added.

items: Laminate: kitchens, children's rooms, rental homes and busy wardrobes
Veneer: living-room feature walls, study furniture, main doors and showpiece pieces
Combine both: veneer on visible fronts and laminate inside or on the back

content.text: If you are torn, bring your layout and we will help you spend on veneer only where it will be seen.
